conventions.convention: Use signature (−+++), length coordinates x⁰=ct, μ≥0 in inverse metres, and □=−∂₀²+Σⱼ∂ⱼ². For μ>0, m_rest,SI=ℏμ/c; μ=0 is the separately admitted massless branch.
The future-shell density is d³k/((2π)³2ωμ), with the massless apex omitted. The shell restriction uses Kμf(p)=∫f(x)e^{i(p⁰x⁰−p⃗·x⃗)}d⁴x, without a prefactor.

The Fock pairing is second-variable-linear; creation is linear and annihilation conjugate-linear in the one-particle argument. Φμ(f)=a(Kμ conjugate(f))+a†(Kμf) acts on the common finite-particle domain.
Assume Countable Choice throughout the inspected Fock and Fourier constructions.
The Hamiltonian is the vacuum-subtracted maximal multiplier ℏc dΓs(ωμ), in joules, with zero vacuum-sector multiplier; no infinite zero-point-energy sum is included.
Scalar Weyl operators use WSegal(√2Kμf). The time-ordered carrier uses the specified partial spatial Fourier extension, without an additional prefactor i, and satisfies (□−μ²)Hμ=iδ₀.
Spacelike separation requires every difference of support points to be spacelike. The example uses μ=0 and nonnegative compact smooth spacetime tests of unit m⁻³.

load_bearing.statement: Under Countable Choice and the selected real-scalar model adoption, define Φμ(f)=a(Kμ conjugate(f))+a†(Kμf) on the bosonic finite-particle domain and Hμphys=ℏc dΓs(ωμ) on the displayed maximal sector-multiplier domain, for μ≥0.

Conditional on the scalar model adoption and Countable Choice: real Schwartz-smeared fields are essentially self-adjoint, obey the tested Klein–Gordon equation and Poincare covariance, have the stated vacuum covariance and forward-cone translation spectrum; spacelike-separated compact tests commute, as do their bounded local Weyl algebras. The Hamiltonian is nonnegative, with positive spectral infimum ℏcμ for μ>0 and no gap for μ=0.

Conditional on the scalar model adoption, Countable Choice and the exact model: ordered real-test vacuum moments vanish for odd n and are sums over pairings for even n; the Weyl expectation is exp(−‖Kμf‖²/2). The specified tempered time-ordered carrier satisfies (□−μ²)Hμ=iδ₀ without an additional prefactor i.

concerns.concern: The Statement says the Hamiltonian 'has Ω as its unique zero-energy vector.' Literally, every scalar multiple of Ω is also a zero-energy vector. Step 2.1 correctly proves that the zero-energy eigenspace is exactly the vacuum sector. State that eigenspace as ℂΩ, or express uniqueness of the vacuum state up to phase.

seams_checked.note: Checked the consuming scalar definition and both theorem assumptions against the supplying page and post-qft-free-field-model. They retain the adopted scalar bosonic representation, zero-particle vacuum, massless/massive branches, units and Countable Choice. The Klein–Gordon field equation is derived locally from shell support rather than attributed to physical adoption as a proof. Both pages preserve conditional model scope and make no empirical-universality or general spin-statistics claim.
